jobs.description:
About The Company

Guidehouse is a leading management, consulting, and technology firm dedicated to helping organizations navigate complex challenges and achieve their strategic objectives. With a focus on innovation and excellence, Guidehouse serves a diverse range of clients across the public and private sectors, including federal agencies, state and local governments, and commercial enterprises. The company prides itself on fostering an inclusive and collaborative work environment that promotes professional growth, diversity, and community engagement. Through its commitment to integrity and delivering impactful solutions, Guidehouse continues to be a trusted partner for organizations seeking to transform their operations and leverage data-driven insights.

About The Role

The Data Scientist position at Guidehouse offers an exciting opportunity for professionals passionate about harnessing data to drive strategic decision-making and operational efficiency. In this role, you will be an integral part of the AI & Data team, working closely with federal government clients to develop and implement advanced analytics solutions. Your expertise will support mission-critical initiatives by designing data visualizations, developing dashboards, and creating scalable data science models that translate complex data sets into actionable insights. This position requires a blend of technical proficiency, analytical thinking, and strong communication skills to effectively collaborate with stakeholders and deliver impactful results. As part of the team, you will contribute to organizational success by optimizing workflows, automating processes, and supporting business development efforts through innovative data solutions.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate must possess the ability to obtain and maintain a Federal or DoD "Public Trust" clearance. A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related STEM discipline is required. Candidates should have at least one year of experience in business analytics, data analysis, data engineering, data visualization, or data science roles. Demonstrated proficiency in SQL, Python, R, and data transformation techniques is essential. Familiarity with dashboard tools such as Tableau or Power BI, as well as cloud-based analytics environments like Databricks, Snowflake, or Impala, is highly desirable. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences are critical for success in this role.

Responsibilities

Design and develop data visualization dashboards and reporting solutions using Tableau to provide comprehensive analytics insights tailored to client needs.
Lead and review data cleaning and transformation scripts utilizing tools such as Databricks, SQL, and Python, ensuring data quality and consistency.
Maintain and enhance existing dashboards, analytics solutions, and reporting tools that support operational and strategic decision-making processes.
Identify opportunities for workflow automation and process optimization, contributing to the implementation of efficient data handling practices.
Collaborate with stakeholders to define, develop, and deliver AI and analytics use cases, translating business requirements into scalable data science solutions.
Support client service initiatives by providing technical expertise, conducting presentations, and explaining complex analytics concepts to diverse audiences.
Participate in business development activities, including preparing proposals, responding to RFPs, and contributing to white papers and thought leadership content.
Engage in ongoing professional development to stay current with emerging data science techniques, tools, and industry best practices.

Benefits

Guidehouse offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support the well-being and professional growth of its employees. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; personal and family sick time; and company-paid holidays. The role may be eligible for a discretionary variable incentive bonus. Employees also enjoy parental leave, adoption assistance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company matching. Additional benefits encompass basic and supplemental life insurance, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts for dental, vision, and dependent care, as well as short-term and long-term disability coverage. The company supports educational advancement through tuition reimbursement, skills development programs, and certifications. Other perks include an employee referral program, community outreach initiatives, emergency backup childcare, and mobility stipends, all aimed at fostering a supportive and engaging work environment.

Equal Opportunity

Guidehouse is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diversity and equal opportunity for all employees and applicants. The company provides accommodations for individuals with disabilities or those requiring assistance during the application process. Guidehouse does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. The company encourages qualified candidates from all backgrounds to apply and join its mission to deliver innovative solutions that make a difference in communities and organizations worldwide.

Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

About The Indiana Department Of Transportation

The Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) provides a dynamic workplace that serves Indiana citizens, improves our state’s quality of life, and enhances its economic opportunity. INDOT has a number of innovative programs and projects, including Public-Private Partnerships, Green Initiatives, and cutting-edge uses of materials and assets. Whether you are an established professional in the transportation field or just starting your career, INDOT has exciting and challenging opportunities for you.

The INDOT District Geologist supports transportation projects by evaluating subsurface conditions, conducting geologic and material assessments, and ensuring geotechnical risks are identified early in project development. The role includes serving as a liaison for the Certified Aggregate Producer Program (CAPP), coordinating with producers to maintain material quality, and performing routine quarry visits to assess aggregate sources and document geologic conditions. Key responsibilities also involve providing technical expertise to engineers, contributing to design recommendations, and supporting construction activities through field investigations and material evaluations. The top three skills sought in an ideal candidate are strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities, effective communication and collaboration with diverse stakeholders, and solid technical knowledge of geology, soil mechanics, and aggregate production.

Location:

This position is in INDOT's LaPorte District

The salary for this position traditionally starts at $59,800.00 but may be commensurate with education and work experience. Use our Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Provide geologic consultation utilizing technical expertise regarding engineering geology, hydrogeology, and geology.
Understand, interpret, and employ applicable State and Federal regulatory rules, guidance, and policies related to geological investigations and contaminant remediation.
Lead or assist field teams during site investigations.
Evaluate and assist in developing geologically related plans and documents.
Develop and write technical reports and correspondence including tabulating and interpreting data for reports.
Follow proper sampling procedures and use appropriate geophysical and other field techniques.
Review and evaluate technical guidance documents, reports, journals, and related articles.
Determine historic geologic and hydrogeologic conditions utilizing agency files.
Assist in geological enforcement actions.
Provide technical assistance to other staff, state and federal agencies, industries, contractors, and the public.

These additional duties may be performed if this position is at the Indiana Department of Natural Resources (DNR)

Perform complex data analysis and interpretation to determine locations and extent of underground sources of drinking water.

Administer INDOT’s Certified Aggregate Producers Program (CAPP) program at the District level. Regulate and monitor all aggregate sources assigned to the District and ensure compliance with Department specifications and guidelines.

Licensed Professional Geologist in Indiana preferred.
Extensive knowledge of the principles, practices, theories, and methodologies applied to geologic/hydrogeologic science and related fields.
Thorough knowledge of and the ability to interpret and apply all applicable federal and state laws, environmental regulations, acts, and guidelines.

Ability to determine resolutions and new approaches to various geotechnical problems.

Specialized knowledge of well hydraulics, ground water modeling, drinking water management, waste and wastewater management, and related regulations.

About The Indiana Department Of Transportation

The Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) provides a dynamic workplace that serves Indiana citizens, improves our state’s quality of life, and enhances its economic opportunity. INDOT has a number of innovative programs and projects, including Public-Private Partnerships, Green Initiatives, and cutting-edge uses of materials and assets. Role Overview

The INDOT District Geologist supports transportation projects by evaluating subsurface conditions, conducting geologic and material assessments, and ensuring geotechnical risks are identified early in project development. The role includes serving as a liaison for the Certified Aggregate Producer Program (CAPP), coordinating with producers to maintain material quality, and performing routine quarry visits to assess aggregate sources and document geologic conditions. Key responsibilities also involve providing technical expertise to engineers, contributing to design recommendations, and supporting construction activities through field investigations and material evaluations. The top three skills sought in an ideal candidate are strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities, effective communication and collaboration with diverse stakeholders, and solid technical knowledge of geology, soil mechanics, and aggregate production.

Location:

This position is in INDOT's LaPorte District

Provide geologic consultation utilizing technical expertise regarding engineering geology, hydrogeology, and geology.
Understand, interpret, and employ applicable State and Federal regulatory rules, guidance, and policies related to geological investigations and contaminant remediation.
Lead or assist field teams during site investigations.
Evaluate and assist in developing geologically related plans and documents.
Develop and write technical reports and correspondence including tabulating and interpreting data for reports.

Review and evaluate technical guidance documents, reports, journals, and related articles.

Financial Disclosure

Essential Job Functions

The AOC HR Data Analyst provides support to the Assistant State Court Administrator- Human Resources and Deputy Director of Human Resources to develop, implement, and assist with the coordination of organizational development. This position serves as a primary contact for strategic planning and a resource for information pertaining to each unit within Human Resources, which include Employee Relations and Compliance; Benefits and Compensation; HRIS Administration; Talent Acquisition; and Judicial Services, and Information Privacy. The incumbent of this position also supports projects from each unit, ensuring the scope of work is met and there is solution driven work for tasks. The day-to-day tasks include but are not limited to organizing data, developing proposals, communicating with internal and external stakeholders, and implementing process improvement initiatives for Human Resources.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Conducts independent business analysis from a human resources perspective for the Maryland Judiciary.

Generates and compiles monthly metrics and analytics and assess data to support the strategic initiatives of the Assistant State Court Administrator- Human Resources and Deputy Director, Human Resources.

Analyzes internal HR processes, procedures, and resources for HR staff.

Coordinates the design and implementation of proactive initiatives, action plans, programs, and training for HR staff.

Analyzes data for external departments within the Administrative Office of the Courts and provides updates.

Works closely with Research and Analysis for reports needed for the State Court Administrator.

Create data dashboards in HRIS system for Human Resources and State Court Administrator to review.

Assists in the development of plans impacting various internal and external stakeholders.

Assists Assistant State Court Administrator- Human Resources and Deputy Director with special projects that impact on the organization (i.e., salary scale updates, financial disclosures, employee engagement initiatives, benefits, employee relations matters)

Collaborate and recommend to HR leadership the development of retention methods based on analysis of information.

Meets with HR leadership and external stakeholders to develop methods to analyze employee engagement and retention methods.

Recommends new initiatives for employee programs.

Assists with project management and development for employee programs.

Review trends and collaborate with teams to execute communications for organizational development.

Develops surveys and works in conjunction with Research and Analysis to analyze data and methodologies to apply for retention purposes.

Monitors communication with external stakeholders to identify proactive approaches and recommend interventions as appropriate.

Implement data dashboards to be used for internal and external factors regarding employee retention and engagement.

Provides Judiciary-wide PIN management in concert with Benefits and Compensation, Talent Acquisition, and Budget.

Completes weekly reports for the active and vacant position reports and distribute to the appropriate parties.

Independently completes the Judiciary Vacancy report to be reviewed by HR leadership and the State Court Administrator.

Reviews the PIN distribution throughout the Judiciary and recommends position changes to align with the strategic initiatives.

Direct support to HR Leadership and Managers of HR Units

Assists Assistant State Court Administrator- HR and Deputy Director HR with identifying legislature impacts pertinent to Human Resources (such as FAMLI, Workplace Violence, leave programs).

Monitor communications with external stakeholders to identify proactive approaches and recommend interventions as appropriate.

Provides direct support as needed for technical assistance within each HR unit.

Gathers and coordinates data associated with data requests from various entities internal and external to the Judiciary.

Assists with research and coordination efforts on various projects related judges, judicial officers, and employees.

Perform other duties as assigned by Assistant State Court Administrator, HR and Deputy Director.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor?s degree from an accredited college or university.

Experience:
Three (3) years of professional human resources experience. One (1) year with data analytics experience.

Preferred:
(1) year of extensive use in Microsoft Excel.

Note:
Additional professional human resources experience as defined above may be substituted on a year-for-year basis for up to four (4) years of the required education.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of:

Human resources policies and procedures, and federal, state, and other applicable human resources related laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances specifically related to employment, benefits, and retirements.

Policies and practices of the Maryland Judiciary.

The use and application of Human Resource Information Systems.

Human resources unit roles and responsibilities.

Techniques used in collecting, tabulating, evaluating, and presenting data.

Word processing, databases, spreadsheet, and graphic computer software applications.

Human resources management theories, policies, and practices.

Analytical procedures and techniques used in organizing and conducting studies and analyses of jobs, organizations, work methods, programs, and operations.

Skill In

Analyzing data to ensure system integrity.

Troubleshooting to resolve issues.

Running and monitoring system processes to update employee records and other business processes.

Using Microsoft Office products to include, but not limited to Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.

Ability To

Interpret and apply policies, procedures, regulations, and laws.

Develop, implement, and administer policies and procedures for effective and efficient HR programs and services.

Independently identify, respond to, and resolve management issues, concerns, and needs related to HRIS.

Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions and exercise good judgment, flexibility, creativity, and sensitivity.

Apply and demonstrate strong analytical and organizational skills.

Provide guidance and accurate information to managers, staff, and administrative heads.

Maintain a harmonious and effective working relationship with supervisors, subordinates, public officials, and the general public.

Plan, develop, and execute activities and functions in assigned program areas.

Coordinate work with other Human Resources units, court locations, and external departments and agencies.

Communicate effectively in writing and orally, including presenting information to large groups.

Operate a personal computer.

Physical Requirements

Perform all essential functions of the position.

Sedentary work

. Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

Equipment, Machinery And Tools

Desktop and general office equipment.

Software And Computer Skills

PeopleSoft based HRIS. Microsoft Office products ? Word, Excel, and Outlook, process mapping software.

Selection Process

Your application package will be used to determine your eligibility, qualifications, and ranking for this position. If you are determined to be ineligible or not qualified, your application will receive no further consideration. It is essential that you provide complete and accurate information on your application. Please report all related education, experience, dates, and hours of work. If you have held more than one (1) position at the same employer, you must list each position that you held, the length of time that you held each position, and the corresponding duties. Description of duties that state, "see resume" will negatively impact consideration for this position. Applicants will not be contacted for additional information. Only applicants considered for this position will be contacted.

Complete applications must be submitted by the closing date. Information submitted after this date will not be added. Incomplete applications will not be accepted. Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed application.

new_jobs.title: Administrative Program Coordinator - Health Access and Community Enrichment (HACE)
new_jobs.description:
Join the transformative team at City of Hope, where we're changing lives and making a real difference in the fight against cancer, diabetes, and other life-threatening illnesses. City of Hope’s growing national system includes its Los Angeles campus, a network of clinical care locations across Southern California, a new cancer center in Orange County, California, and treatment facilities in Atlanta, Chicago and Phoenix. Our dedicated and compassionate employees are driven by a common mission: To deliver the cures of tomorrow to the people who need them today.

Position Summary:

This position performs a variety of administrative duties and analytical functions to support the daily operations of the Health Access and Community Enrichment (HACE) department. The work assignments are often complex, diversified, and confidential which requires one to be highly responsible, tactful, and professional. Being successful in this role requires excellent organizational skills, meticulous attention to detail, and flexibility in order to support the needs of the department. The Program Coordinator is a highly organized, self‑motivated professional who independently manages multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast‑paced environment while building effective partnerships with internal clients, stakeholders, external partners, and staff at all levels of the organization.

As a successful candidate, you will:

Provide executive-level administrative support to Chief HACE Officer, including complex calendar management, meeting scheduling, travel and itinerary coordination, and expense tracking.
Assists in the daily administrative functions of managing an effective department. Uses discretionary initiative and judgment in handling sensitive and confidential details, establishing priorities and resolving problems relating to daily operations and administrative detail of a highly functioning department in the daily administrative functions of managing an effective department.
Assists in department business activities, including but not limited to: budget preparation and monitoring; account management; purchasing; personnel; facilities; travel and reporting required by the institution. Participates in short and long-range planning and policy or program development by analyzing operational policies, resource utilization, etc. and developing recommendations for department management.
Oversees expenditures within established limits. Understands, communicates, and monitors budget activities and analyzes variances/targets.
Organizes and expedites flow of work, initiating follow up action as appropriate. Coordinates and maintains department policy/procedure and supports executive leadership in select projects/programs, providing project management, communications and presentation/materials support,
Coordinates departmental projects and events including faculty symposiums, research forums, and engagement activities.
Completes expense reports/requisitions/check requests in ERP (which will require being knowledgeable of institutional and extramural funding policies and procedures).

Your qualifications should include:

Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience may substitute for minimum education requirements
3 or more years of progressively responsible experience in business administration, clinical research or healthcare environment

City of Hope employees pay is based on the following criteria: work experience, qualifications, and work location.
